newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ITALIAN SERIE A MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ITALIAN SERIE A MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.

text.p: Italian Serie A matches scheduled for Sunday (league positions in parentheses, all kick-off times 14.30 GMT):

Bologna's surprise 5-1 drubbing by Perugia on Thursday may give hope to Vicenza. Both teams are among nine sides still in the battle for four UEFA Cup qualifying places and both will be without a key player -- Uruguyan Marcelo Otero of Vicenza and Russian Igor Kolyvanov of Bologna, both injured.

Leaders Juventus come into this top of the table clash with a comfortable six point lead with three games to play and can thus clinch the title with a win. Their morale is high following their 4-1 win against Piacenza on Thursday, while Parma may be deflated after their 1-1 home draw with AC Milan. Ciro Ferrara returns in defence, while Croat Alen Boksic, Christian Vieri, Nicola Amoruso and Alessandro Del Piero are all available in attack. Parma will be without suspended defender Antonio Benarrivo and injured Croat midfielder Mario Stanic but field Argentine Hernan Crespo and Enrico Chiesa in attack.

Milan are still five points outside the UEFA Cup qualifying zone and need a win. In-form Lazio, 3-2 winners against Napoli on Thursday, are unlikely to do them any favours. Giuseppe Signori and Pierluigi Casiraghi lead the Lazio attack, while Roberto Baggio and George Weah are up front for Milan who will be without suspended captain Franco Baresi.

Napoli will fancy their chances against a Fiorentina side whose current lack of motivation was all too apparent in a 4-1 defeat by Cagliari on Thursday. Napoli will be without suspended midfielder Fabio Pecchia but field Brazilian midfielder Beto behind Nicola Caccia and Alfredo Aglietti in attack. Fiorentina are without injured Portuguese midfielder Rui Costa while their prospects of qualifying for the UEFA Cup are more mathematical than realistic.

This will be a real bone-cruncher between two of three sides -- Perugia are the third -- involved in a relegation battle which will probably see two of them go down. Piacenza got run over 4-1 by the high speed Juventus train on Thursday but will put that behind them against Cagliari, like them on 33 points. Pasquale Luiso and Gian Pietro Piovani seem sure to lead the Piacenza attack, while Cagliari may field the three-man attack of Uruguyan Dario Silva, Roberto Muzzi and Sandro Tovalieri which did well in that 4-1 win against Fiorentina on Thursday.

Perugia's surprise 5-1 win against Bologna on Thursday has kept alive their hopes of Serie A survival and they could take another step along that path by beating bottom side Reggiana, already relegated. Perugia defender Giacomo Dicara is suspended while striker Marco Negri, scorer of a hat-trick against Bologna, will want to maintain that form.

UEFA Cup finalists Inter could overtake Parma in the battle for second place if they win here and Parma lose to Juventus in Turin. Injuries leave Inter with little option but to field their first choice strike force of Frenchman Youri Djorkaeff behind Maurizo Ganz and Chilean Ivan Zamorano. Having picked up their first league win for two months when beating Atalanta 4-0 away on Thursday, Roma are likely to prove awkward, with Argentine striker Abel Balbo and Francesco Totti leading their front line. Roma midfielders, Swede Jonas Thern and Francesco Statuto are both suspended.

This game could be decisive for the UEFA Cup prospects of both sides, separated by only two points. Udinese will be without suspended full-back Raffaele Sergio while Brazilian striker Amoroso is doubtful because of a shoulder injury. Udinese can however still field an attack comprising German Oliver Bierhoff and Paolo Poggi, scorer of two goals in a 3-0 win against Verona on Thursday. Sampdoria, held to a 1-1 away draw by Vicenza in midweek, again look to captain Roberto Mancini and Vincenzo Montella in attack.

Atalanta ought to pick up the points against a Verona side seemingly destined for relegation. Serie A's leading goalscorer Filippo Inzaghi, on the 20 mark, might use the occasion to get back on the scoresheet.
